stepsClear.summary: Stops the step engine and removes its definitions so a new sequence can be built.
prerequisites: Import Steps & Transitions and its declared dependencies.

examples.title: Use clear step definitions
examples.explanation: Block notation: Stops the step engine and removes its definitions so a new sequence can be built. Command; errors are displayed.

notes: GRAFCET-inspired logical steps, not a safety controller or standards-compliance claim. Define numbered steps 1–16 and transitions 1–24 while stopped; choose at least one initial step. Start activates initial steps. Before each explicit scan, set current transition conditions. Scan clears them, so provide fresh values every cycle. A scan uses the old active-step snapshot: new targets cannot cascade immediately. Lowest transition number wins a source-step conflict; independent transitions fire together. Advanced groups support fork/join and a minimum time in source steps (0–86400000 ms). Activation wins simultaneous activation/deactivation. Elapsed time restarts on reentry. Entry/exit describe the latest scan only. Stop/reset makes all steps inactive and clears inputs; clear also removes configuration. No pins, motors or outputs are changed automatically. Local native build and host tests only; physical execution awaits firmware approval.
Source: integration\Steps_Transitions.ubl. Examples are illustrative block notation, not hardware acceptance tests.

examples.explanation: Block notation: Defines a numbered transition from one step to another while stopped. Command; transition numbers are 1 through 24.

examples.title: Two-step sequence
examples.code:
clear step definitions
define step [1] initial [true]
define step [2] initial [false]
transition [1] step [1] to [2]
start steps
transition [1] condition [true]
advance one step scan
step [2] active?
examples.explanation: The final test is true if configuration succeeds. Conditions are consumed by the scan, and no pins or motors are changed automatically.
